intro: Lesson 4: A world war: the Indian Army and Muslim soldiers. To understand the global nature of the First World War and the contribution of soldiers from the Empire, including Muslims

questions.q: Why is it called a 'world' war?
questions.a: It was fought on several continents and seas, with soldiers from empires across the world
questions.model: Where: Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the seas. Who: soldiers from Britain, France and their empires. So it was worldwide.

questions.q: Name two places outside Europe where the Indian Army fought.
questions.a: For example: Mesopotamia and East Africa (or Gallipoli)

questions.q: Where is the Muslim burial ground for First World War soldiers in England?
Core: In the portal response box, write a short biography of Khudadad Khan and explain why his story matters.
questions.a: Muslim soldier from Punjab; bravery at Hollebeke, 31 October 1914; first Indian VC; matters because it shows the Empire's and Muslims' contribution
questions.model: Teacher shows the first sentence: 'Khudadad Khan was a Muslim soldier from Punjab in the Indian Army.'

questions.q: Extend: Why were the contributions of Empire soldiers often overlooked?
questions.a: Histories focused on British soldiers on the Western Front; few records or memorials told their stories

questions.q: Stretch: How can historians recover forgotten stories?
questions.a: Letters, army records, hospital records, memorials and family memories

questions.q: Big question: why is it called a world war, and whose stories are often forgotten?
questions.a: It was fought across the world; the stories of Indian, African and other Empire soldiers, including Muslims, were often forgotten
